correctness.rationale: The fixed set is the union of the two lattices with only their common double zero at 0. The dot-product bound on the derivative of the product is strict at every real point (the two equality phases would impose a rational pi), while the derivative correction samples arbitrarily close to -2pi already at half-integers. Thus the endpoint gain is included. Monotonicity traps each orbit between fixed points and makes its iterates monotone; the signs on the complementary intervals give the exact neighboring-endpoint basins, including attraction to 0 only from the left. Each of the two multiplier phases is an irrational rotation, with densities 2 and 2/pi. The admissible negative-sine angular fraction is arcsin(min(1,2/amplitude))/pi, with null boundary. This verifies the normalized mixture, the unnormalized sink density and its two one-sided cusp coefficients; the newly affected families do not attain -1 at their cusp thresholds. The computed D(0.7) is 0.6188372299438043. In t=2x coordinates an interior j*pi can affect only its own integer interval (these intervals are separated). Conditional on either parity class of j, j*pi modulo 2 is uniform, so the parity selecting repellers leaves the fractional offset uniform. Per unit t, pi-lattice sinks give density 1/(2pi) at width 1, flanking integer sinks give density 1/pi at widths 1+u and 2-u, and the other integer sinks give density 1/2-1/pi at width 2. Dividing widths by two and normalizing by the total yields exactly the stated atoms and continuous component; the origin and window boundary have vanishing weight.
residual_risks: The finite width diagnostic tests masses and the continuous component's mean, not uniformity; that law follows from the analytic parity argument.
No effective discrepancy estimate or description of non-fixed attractors is established. The window counts locations, not initial-state mass.

value.rationale: The exact per-sink basin distribution answers a concrete prevalence question in a published multistability model. It exposes two discrete geometries and a continuous one, and the sharp distinction between loss of order and two later losses of sink density gives testable spatial predictions. These are substantive map-specific facts beyond an isolated application of equidistribution.
residual_risks: These are spatial fixed-point statistics; they do not determine outcomes under an arbitrary initial distribution or prevalence of attracting cycles.
